$comment: How strict the gate is (workflow/tools/lib/levels.mjs). Yours to edit, never the agent's: it may propose a change, you make it. phase: prototype (nothing outside depends on it: structure checks only advise, /ship runs the tests the change reaches), pilot (a few real people or their data: untested code, docs and errors fail again, /ship runs everything) or production (it takes money or people rely on it: every check fails; a production deploy needs this phase). direction.goals (optional): where the goals to work towards come from, in order (requests, parts, health, areas, feedback, signals); without it the phase decides (workflow/tools/lib/focus.mjs DIRECTION: the product itself in a prototype, what users report first in a pilot, what the running app reports first in production). npm run phase says which one the facts fit and what the next one still needs. checks: a quality check's level, fail, advise or off, over the phase's; the safety stops (secrets, signoff, migrations, the tests...) have none. process: from which card size (always, small, medium, large, never) a spec, a pitch, a UI board and a fresh review at /ship are needed (spec, pitch, uiBoard, review), and the user guide and app map are kept up in the card itself (upkeep; below it they wait for one /docs catch-up pass), and /spec has two designs drafted apart before it chooses one (designs: large cards in a pilot and in production, none in a prototype; in every phase /spec also drafts two when a card adds a flow or a job, gives a job a second home, or is a step back after a run of fixes). reach: chain (every test that leans on a change, the default) or direct (only the tests importing a changed file: faster, GitHub still runs them all). cache: picked (a picked test that passed on this computer with the same code is skipped, the default) or all (the whole suite too: --all and a pilot or production /ship; GitHub always runs everything). The gate prints what is loosened on every run.
